display.title: Episode 17: The Star Gazer, Chapter 2 (Before Pesach)
display.summary_short: A stargazer learns why a young man he expected to die came out of the forest alive: a piece of bread given to a starving man. Plus a Pesach niggun, Shema with a guest from Yerushalayim, and letters.
display.summary_long: Aired the week before Pesach 5742. Uncle Yossi opens with a joyful five-word Yom Tov niggun about being happy on the holiday, then announces a Tzivos Hashem Pesach Experience Fair for Chol HaMoed. Story time continues The Star Gazer: a stargazer had predicted that a young man would not come back alive from the forest, yet he returned happy. Before the chapter, a special guest from Yerushalayim recites the Shema. The stargazer asks the young man what happened, and he recalls a starving old man who begged for food; as he opened his sack to share his bread, a snake leaped out and slithered away. The stargazer explains that his life was spared by a power greater than the stars. Uncle Yossi teaches Shlomo HaMelech's words, 'tzedakah saves from death', and that tzedakah brings Hashem's blessings. The show also promotes a shmurah matzah film narrated by Uncle Yossi, reads a letter with a riddle about 'maasim tovim', and includes a phone call in which Uncle Yossi finds the word Ashrei in a boy's names. It ends with Dial-a-Jewish-Story and a suggestion for an afikoman present.
display.lesson: Tzedakah saves from death: giving to someone in need brings Hashem's protection and blessings.

date.note: 'Pesach is just around the corner'; fair on Sunday April 11 in Chol HaMoed Pesach 5742; one week before episode 18 (1982-04-06).
